oneLiner: 使命答“我们为谁创造什么价值”，愿景绘“我们想成为的未来”，价值观定“我们坚守的原则”。
oneLinerEn: Mission says what value we create for whom; vision paints the future we want; values fix the principles we keep.
detail: 这三者是全组织决策的上位判据：当战略取舍、资源分配两难时，能回到“是否符合使命、是否朝愿景靠近、有没有违反价值观”来判断。空泛口号没人信，好的使命愿景具体到能被拿来否决一个赚钱的机会。
detailEn: These three are the master criteria above every decision: when strategy or resource allocation gets contentious, you return to 'does it serve the mission, move toward the vision, honour our values'. Slogans ring hollow; a good mission and vision are concrete enough to veto a profitable opportunity.

oneLiner: 把局面摊成四格：优势与劣势(内部)、机会与威胁(外部)。
oneLinerEn: Lay the situation out in four boxes: strengths and weaknesses (inside), opportunities and threats (outside).
detail: SWOT 便宜、直观、门槛低，是战略讨论的好起点。常见毛病是列完就停、四格平铺不分主次，或者把模糊感觉写成“优势”。真正有用的是进一步组合成行动：如何用优势抓机会、如何补短避威，并从中排出优先级。
detailEn: SWOT is cheap, intuitive and an easy entry point to strategic talk. Its failure mode is stopping at four undifferentiated boxes, or dressing vague feelings as 'strengths'. The value is in the combinations — matching strength to opportunity, fixing weakness against threat — and then prioritising.

oneLiner: 判断一个行业赚不赚钱：现有竞争、潜在进入、替代品、供应商议价力、买方议价力。
oneLinerEn: Judge an industry's profit potential by five forces: rivalry, new entrants, substitutes, supplier power, buyer power.
detail: 迈克尔·波特 (1979) 把“竞争”从对对手的盯梢，升级为对整个行业结构的理解。五股力量越强，行业回报越被瓜分侵蚀。战略的意义因此是：选一个结构有利的位置，或用行动改变这些力量本身(如提高转换成本、构筑壁垒)。
detailEn: Michael Porter (1979) widened 'competition' from watching rivals to understanding industry structure. The stronger the five forces, the more profit gets competed away. Strategy then means occupying a structurally favourable position — or changing the forces themselves, say by raising switching costs or building barriers.

oneLiner: 要么更便宜(成本领先)，要么更特别(差异化)，要么更聚焦；卡在中间最难活。
oneLinerEn: Lead on cost, differentiate, or focus — being stuck in the middle is the hardest way to survive.
detail: 波特认为企业必须在三种连贯定位中选择其一：在全行业以更低成本取胜、以独特性获得溢价、或收缩到某个细分战场。最怕“夹在中间”：既没有成本优势，也没有鲜明的差异化，容易被两头挤压。取舍(Trade-off)是战略的灵魂——决定不做什么，和做什么同样重要。
detailEn: Porter held that a firm must pursue one coherent position: win on cost across the industry, command a premium through uniqueness, or narrow to a segment. The fatal spot is 'stuck in the middle' — neither low-cost nor distinctive, squeezed from both sides. Trade-offs are the soul of strategy: deciding what not to matters as much as what to.

oneLiner: 从政治、经济、社会、技术、环境、法律六个方向，看组织外部的长期大势。
oneLinerEn: Watch six external currents shaping the long game: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, Legal.
detail: PESTEL 是识别机会与威胁来源的清单，常与 SWOT 的外部两格配合。它的价值不在填满六格，而在追问“这条趋势对我们意味着什么、我们会因此改变什么”，把宏观信号翻译成具体决策。
detailEn: PESTEL is a checklist for where opportunities and threats arise, often feeding the two external boxes of a SWOT. Its worth is not in filling six cells but in the follow-up: 'so what does this trend mean for us, and what will we change', turning macro signals into concrete decisions.

oneLiner: 用鼓舞人心的目标(O)加两三个可量化、有时限的关键结果(KR)，让全组织朝同一方向聚焦。
oneLinerEn: An inspiring Objective plus two or three measurable, time-bound Key Results keep the whole organisation pointed one way.
detail: 由安迪·格鲁夫在英特尔成形、约翰·杜尔在《Measure What Matters》推广。要义：少而聚焦、上下对齐又高度透明、敢于设定“野心目标”(拿到约七成即算优秀)，把它与绩效考核适度脱钩以鼓励冒险。若 KR 全是“照常运营”，就退化成了任务清单。
detailEn: Shaped by Andy Grove at Intel and popularised by John Doerr in Measure What Matters. The essentials: few and focused, aligned yet highly visible, bold enough that hitting ~70% counts as good, and kept partly separate from pay reviews so people will reach. If every KR is 'business as usual', it has decayed into a to-do list.

oneLiner: 不去血腥的红海硬拼，而是用“价值创新”开创让竞争无关的新市场空间。
oneLinerEn: Rather than battle in a bloody red ocean, use value innovation to open a market space that makes competition irrelevant.
detail: 钱·金与勒内·莫博涅 (2005) 提出“四步动作框架”：哪些被行业视为理所当然的要素可以剔除或减少、哪些应当提升或创造，从而同时压低成本的曲线、抬高价值的曲线。关键不是技术颠覆，而是重新定义问题与买家。
detailEn: W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne (2005) offer the four-actions framework: which taken-for-granted factors to eliminate or reduce, and which to raise or create — lowering the cost curve while lifting the value curve at once. The point is not technological disruption but redefining the problem and the buyer.

oneLiner: 真正的护城河是能横跨多种产品、难以模仿、为客户带来显著价值的“能力根”。
oneLinerEn: The real moat is a root capability that spans products, is hard to imitate and delivers customer value.
detail: 普拉哈拉德与哈默尔 (1990) 用“树”作比喻：终端产品是叶子，核心竞争力是树根。多元化应围绕核心能力生长(本田的发动机能力延伸到摩托、汽车、发电机)，而不是追着一个热概念乱铺摊子。判断一条能力够不够“核心”：可延展、难模仿、客户可感知价值。
detailEn: Prahalad and Hamel (1990) used the tree: end products are the leaves, core competences the roots. Diversification should grow out of a competence that spans markets (Honda's engines reach motorcycles, cars, generators) rather than chasing whichever concept is hot. Test a competence for extension across products, difficulty of imitation, and value to customers.

oneLiner: 把企业拆成从进料到售后的一串活动，看每一环是创造价值还是消耗成本。
oneLinerEn: Break the firm into a chain of activities from inbound logistics to service, and see which link adds value or burns cost.
detail: 迈克尔·波特(1985)区分基本活动(内部后勤、生产、外部后勤、市场销售、服务)与支持活动(基础设施、人力资源、技术、采购)，竞争优势来自比对手更优地设计并执行这条链，或用“链接”把环节咬合成对手难以复制的系统。它把“成本”与“差异化”落到具体活动上。
detailEn: Michael Porter (1985) split primary activities (inbound logistics, operations, outbound logistics, marketing, service) from support activities (infrastructure, HR, technology, procurement). Advantage comes from performing the chain better than rivals, or from linking activities into a system hard to copy. It grounds 'cost' and 'differentiation' in concrete activities.

oneLiner: 用九宫格讲清一家企业如何创造价值、传递价值、获取价值。
oneLinerEn: Nine blocks that state how a firm creates, delivers and captures value.
detail: 奥斯特瓦德提出：客户细分、价值主张、渠道、客户关系、收入来源(前台五格)，加上关键资源、关键活动、关键伙伴与成本结构(后台四格)。它把抽象的“商业模式”变成可讨论、可涂改的一页图，方便比较方案、发现断点(如为低端客户配了高接触渠道)。
detailEn: Osterwalder's canvas: customer segments, value proposition, channels, customer relationships and revenue streams on the front; key resources, key activities, key partnerships and cost structure on the back. It turns an abstract 'business model' into one discussable, erasable page — handy for comparing options and spotting mismatches (a high-touch channel serving low-end customers).

oneLiner: 增长有四条路：市场渗透、市场开发、产品开发、多元化——按新旧产品×新旧市场划分。
oneLinerEn: Four ways to grow — penetrate, develop markets, develop products, or diversify — by pairing new/old products with new/old markets.
detail: 伊戈尔·安索夫(1957)用“产品×市场”两轴四象限给增长选项定位：市场渗透风险最低，产品开发、市场开发渐进，多元化风险最高。它不告诉你该选哪个，但逼你说清“增长到底从哪来”，并直观对应风险阶梯，常与 SWOT 的“机会”衔接。
detailEn: Igor Ansoff (1957) placed growth options in a product-by-market grid: market penetration is the least risky, then product and market development, with diversification the riskiest. It does not pick for you but forces you to say where growth actually comes from, mapping neatly onto a risk ladder and feeding the 'opportunities' box of a SWOT.

oneLiner: 获客、激活、留存、推荐、收入——用五步漏斗衡量增长是否健康。
oneLinerEn: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue — a five-stage funnel for measuring whether growth is healthy.
detail: 戴夫·麦克卢尔为初创企业提出的“海盗指标”，把增长拆成用户生命周期五环，每一环都要有可量化的关键指标(如次日/30 日留存、K 因子、付费转化)。它的价值是逼你为每环设定北极星与阈值，快速定位漏得最狠的一环;留存常被视为“是否有人真正爱用”的照妖镜，前四环最终都要落到收入这一环。
detailEn: Dave McClure's 'pirate metrics' for startups splits growth into five stages of the user lifecycle, each needing a quantifiable key metric (day-1/day-30 retention, K-factor, paid conversion). Its value is forcing a north-star and threshold per stage so you find the leakiest one fast; retention acts as the truth serum for whether anyone actually loves the product, and the first four rings must ultimately land on revenue.

oneLiner: 把业务摆进“增长×份额”四格：明星、现金牛、问题、瘦狗，据此定投资与取舍。
oneLinerEn: Plot each unit on growth x share — Star, Cash Cow, Question Mark or Dog — and let the box set where to invest or cut.
detail: 布鲁斯·亨德森(1970)为波士顿咨询所创：纵轴市场增长率(要不要输血)、横轴相对市场份额(有没有造血)。明星两头高，应加码；现金牛低增长高份额，挤现金去养别人；问题高增长低份额，是赌未来的选择题；瘦狗两头弱，通常剥离。它给多元化公司一张“资金从哪来到哪去”的简明地图；局限是“份额=优势”与“增长=吸引力”并非万能，故常与 GE 九格(改用行业吸引力/竞争力两轴)互补。
detailEn: Bruce Henderson's 1970 matrix for BCG: vertical is market growth (whether to feed cash), horizontal is relative share (whether it generates cash). Stars are high on both — invest; Cash Cows are mature with high share — milk them to fund others; Question Marks grow fast with low share — a bet on the future; Dogs are weak on both — usually divest. It gives a diversified firm a simple map of where money comes from and goes; its limits — that share equals strength and growth equals attractiveness — are why it is often paired with the GE nine-box, which swaps the axes for industry attractiveness and competitive strength.

oneLiner: 同时经营三条时间线：守住核心、押注成长、孵化未来，别让今天的成功饿死明天的机会。
oneLinerEn: Run three timelines at once — defend the core, build the growth, seed the future — so today's success does not starve tomorrow's.
detail: 麦肯锡(巴盖拉等,2004)提出增长的三个视角：第一层是现金核心业务，优化与防守；第二层是正在起量、需重点培育的新增长业务；第三层是不确定但可能改写格局的长期期权与实验。关键不是“三年计划”，而是让三条线各有独立的指标、节奏与负责人，防止资源被第一层全部吃掉，导致公司在主业见顶时后继无人。
detailEn: McKinsey's Three Horizons (Bagarozzi and others, 2004): Horizon 1 is the cash core to optimise and defend, Horizon 2 the fast-rising growth bets to scale, and Horizon 3 the uncertain long-term options that could reshape the game. The point is not a three-year plan but giving each horizon its own metrics, cadence and owner, so the core does not devour all resources and leave the firm stranded when it plateaus.

oneLiner: 产量越大、单位成本越低——固定成本被摊薄，是低价与壁垒的常见来源。
oneLinerEn: The bigger the output, the lower the unit cost — fixed costs spread thin, a classic source of low price and entry barriers.
detail: 规模经济指随产量上升，单位成本因固定投入(设备、研发、模具、平台)被摊薄、采购与议价更划算而下降；这正是工厂、软件与平台的护城河之一，也解释了低价与“赢家通吃”。但有边界：大到一定规模会出现“规模不经济”——层级臃肿、沟通成本与官僚膨胀反噬。它与学习曲线/经验效应相关(越做越熟)，但要区分“大”与“灵活”，精益与模块化正是为了兼得两者。
detailEn: Economies of scale are the fall in unit cost as output rises, because fixed inputs (plant, R&D, tooling, platform) are spread thinner and purchasing gains bargaining power — a moat for factories, software and platforms, and a driver of low prices and winner-takes-all. But there is a limit: past a size come diseconomies of scale — bloated layers, soaring communication cost and a bureaucratic backlash. It is kin to the learning and experience curve (better with repetition), yet 'big' must be weighed against 'nimble' — lean and modularity seek to have both.

oneLiner: 用的人越多、产品对每个人都越值钱——电话、平台与社交网络的增长引擎。
oneLinerEn: The more people use it, the more valuable it becomes to each user — the growth engine of phones, platforms and social networks.
detail: 梅特卡夫定律说网络的价值约与节点数的平方成正比。当新增用户让老用户更受益(如通讯录、市场买卖双方、操作系统的软件生态),就会形成正反馈:越大越好用、越好用越大,常导向“赢家通吃”与高进入壁垒。但要警惕负面网络效应(拥堵、垃圾信息)与“冷启动”难题——先想办法跨过最小临界规模。它常与规模经济、锁定效应相伴,是平台战略的核心。
detailEn: Metcalfe's law holds that a network's value grows roughly with the square of its nodes. When each new user makes the product better for existing ones — contacts, two-sided markets, an operating system's app ecosystem — a positive loop forms: bigger is better and better attracts bigger, often yielding winner-takes-all and high entry barriers. Watch for negative network effects (congestion, spam) and the cold-start problem: you must first cross a minimum critical mass. It travels with economies of scale and lock-in, and sits at the heart of platform strategy.

oneLiner: 增长不是单次猛推,而是让一环推动下一环,飞轮越转越沉、越转越快。
oneLinerEn: Growth is not one big push but each step driving the next — a flywheel that gains momentum turn after turn.
detail: 吉姆·柯林斯在《从优秀到卓越》借飞轮比喻:卓越公司不靠某个“奇迹时刻”,而是把一连串成果沿同一方向持续累积,像重轮一下下推动,起初费力、一旦转起来便势不可挡。亚马逊的经典飞轮是“更低价格→更多顾客→更多卖家→更优规模与体验→再降价”。它提醒:别频繁换方向空转,要找到并死磕那台能自我强化的飞轮。
detailEn: In Good to Great, Collins uses the flywheel: great companies achieve no single 'miracle moment' but compound a sequence of results in one direction, pushing a heavy wheel blow after blow — hard at first, unstoppable once spinning. Amazon's classic loop is lower prices, more customers, more sellers, better scale and experience, then still lower prices. It warns against thrashing between directions: find the one self-reinforcing flywheel and stay on it.

oneLiner: 把抽象战略画成一张因果图:学习成长支撑流程,流程创造客户,客户换来财务。
oneLinerEn: Draw the abstract strategy as one cause-and-effect map: learning fuels processes, processes create customer value, customers deliver financial results.
detail: 卡普兰与诺顿在平衡计分卡之后提出战略地图:用财务、客户、内部流程、学习与成长四个层面,把“价值如何被创造”串成一条自上而下的因果链,让每个部门看到自己的活动如何汇成最终成果。它解决的是“人人认同战略、却说不清自己那一环如何贡献”的执行难题。与平衡计分卡(指标)配套:地图讲逻辑,记分卡给度量。
detailEn: Kaplan and Norton added the strategy map after the balanced scorecard: across the financial, customer, internal-process and learning-and-growth perspectives it strings how value is created into one top-down causal chain, so every unit sees how its activity feeds the outcome. It answers the stalemate of everyone agreeing with the strategy yet unable to say how their link contributes. It pairs with the scorecard — the map tells the logic, the card supplies the measures.

oneLiner: 互联网让无数小众销量的总和,能抵得上甚至超过少数爆款——别只盯着头部。
oneLinerEn: Online, the sum of countless niche sellers can rival or beat a few blockbusters — do not chase only the hits.
detail: 克里斯·安德森(2004)指出:当仓储、分发与搜索的成本趋近于零,货架不再稀缺,那些单量很小、却种类海量的“冷门”商品加起来,能形成与头部热门相抗衡的巨大市场(亚马逊、Netflix、Spotify 靠此)。它依赖三力:普及生产工具、降低分发摩擦、智能筛选推荐。但长尾并非取代头部——需求曲线仍偏斜,爆款依旧存在,策略是“头部引流、尾部获利”兼得。
detailEn: Anderson (2004) argued that when storage, distribution and search fall near zero cost, shelf space stops being scarce, and the vast set of tiny-selling uncommons adds up to a market rivaling the hits (Amazon, Netflix and Spotify ride this). It rests on three forces: proliferate production tools, cut distribution friction, and filter and recommend smartly. But the tail does not replace the head — demand stays skewed and blockbusters endure; the play is to funnel traffic from the head and profit from the tail.
